Owner-approved fresh generation after local repair exhaustion. FRESH IMPLEMENTATION: start from the approved clean base, inspect PR #304 read-only for useful tests, do not carry forward the rejected caching design. First measure actual SQLite VM steps, returned/decoded rows, statements including PRAGMA, and writer-lock work on baseline. Prefer minimal indexed lookup/query improvement and remove duplicate reads without caching mutable gate/session state across decisions. Preserve original activation order and concurrent visibility, especially kill-switch transitions, closure/reopen, deferred retries and unrelated writes. Test one and 26 holdings per tenant at 100 tenants (paused/linked, killed, deferred, thousands of histories), plus 1/10 tenants. Require measurable improvement on target workload and no material regression on other cases; report baseline/new measurements and run tests.test_hotwatch_holdings_auto. If optimization cannot preserve semantics, do not ship regression or claim acceptance.
Prior independent review findings (evidence, not expanded permissions):
- The per-user batch caches session and retry state before SQLite acquires the write lock on the first upsert. If reconciliation commits POSITION_CLOSED for a later holding in that gap, the scan can overwrite the closure using stale state or skip the new generation. Previously, reads for later holdings ran inside the transaction once the first upsert acquired the lock. The 1/10/100-user regression covers tenant scoping and SQL counts but misses this interleaving.
- hotwatch_service.py:849 changes the writer-lock boundary. If another connection commits before BEGIN IMMEDIATE and the refreshed batch needs no write, the scan keeps the writer lock while processing every remaining tenant, even if the tick ultimately writes nothing. The old path acquired that lock only at the first upsert. The 1/10/100-user test covers SQL counts and tenant decisions, but the race test still writes after refresh and misses this contention regression.
- auto_holdings_tick eagerly loads session and retry history for every holding of the current user before evaluating the first candidate. When the first holding can activate, the baseline reads only that holding’s history, so the new path can do substantially more SQL and JSON work even with fewer statements. The 1/10/100-user test forces activation near the end and counts statements, leaving this early-activation regression unmeasured.
- hotwatch_service.py:821–840 regresses SQLite work under the writer lock. In the existing early-activation fixture, make holding 1 link to a PAUSED watch without a prior attempt, leave holding 2 eligible, and seed completed session history for holdings 3–25. The first link acquires the writer lock, then the batch fetches and decodes all later history before activating holding 2. The base skips those later rows. Expected: keep later-history reads bounded on early activation and verify rows read in CI, since statement counts miss this lock-time regression.
- hotwatch_service.py:821–839 adds a SQLite writer-lock regression. Seed one user with a first holding that needs a LINKED write, a second already linked, a third eligible to activate, and later holdings with session and retry history. The tick loads and decodes the entire remaining history while holding SQLite’s writer lock, even though it stops at the third holding. The base stops reading holding history at that activation. Bound the lookahead under the writer lock and cover third-position activation in test_hotwatch_holdings_auto.py.
- hotwatch_service.py:827–863 can miss a concurrent stop. With five holdings whose autowatch rows already match their paused sessions, stop the fifth watch on another connection after the batch SELECTs finish and before the fifth holding is evaluated. The cached PAUSED row makes the scan keep LINKED and return without checking data_version. The base scan re-reads the fifth session, sees COMPLETED, and records STOPPED in that tick. Revalidate cached no-write decisions when the batch has changed and cover this interleaving in test_hotwatch_holdings_auto.py.
- hotwatch_service.py regresses idle SQLite behavior. Seed holdings already LINKED to PAUSED watches with no writes due. During the scan, commit an unrelated row on a second connection, then hold BEGIN IMMEDIATE there through the scan's timeout. The database-wide data_version change makes the idle scan request the writer lock and raise SQLITE_BUSY. Expected behavior is to return None without waiting for the writer because no holding decision changed. The new idle test holds a writer without an intervening commit, so it misses this path.
- hotwatch_service.py:809–873 can retry the same tenant indefinitely. Seed tenant 1 with only already-linked holdings and tenant 2 with a due holding. Commit an unrelated row from a second SQLite connection after each tenant 1 batch read and before the end-of-scan data_version check. Each commit restarts tenant 1 without a retry bound, so tenant 2 and subsequent feed maintenance never run. The prior scan completed under the same schedule. Expected: bounded per-tick work under unrelated commits, while preserving revalidation before any write.
- hotwatch_service.py, auto_holdings_tick: Give tenant A five already-linked PAUSED holdings. Commit an unrelated write after the first scan reads holdings 4–5, then complete holding 5's watch after the refresh reads that batch. The second data_version mismatch leaves holding 5 LINKED and advances to the next tenant. The original per-position loop sees COMPLETED when that commit lands before holding 5's individual lookup and records STOPPED in the same tick. The added tests cover a relevant commit on the first scan and repeated unrelated commits, leaving this regression uncovered.
- hotwatch_service.py regresses the idle 100-user scan. Give each enabled user one fresh holding with a matching PAUSED watch and an existing LINKED record, with no concurrent writes. The base executes 302 scan statements. This change executes 403, including 101 PRAGMA data_version reads, while eliminating zero lookups. Expected: no extra scan statements for this idle workload. The SQL-count test in tests/test_hotwatch_holdings_auto.py counts SELECTs separately from PRAGMAs and starts with a LINKED write, so it misses this path.
- hotwatch_service.py regresses idle-scan SQL work under concurrent writes. Extend test_repeated_unrelated_commits_do_not_starve_next_tenant to 100 tenants with one already-linked holding each and commit an unrelated row update after each autowatch read. The new scan executes 8 statements per tenant (three passes), versus 3 at the base commit, with identical decisions. Expect unrelated commits to preserve the idle-scan read budget while real session or autowatch changes still trigger revalidation.
- hotwatch_service.py: auto_holdings_tick bounds asset keys but fetches and decodes every matching historical session while holding SQLite’s writer lock. Reproduce with holding 1 creating a LINKED row, holdings 2–3 already linked, holding 4 due for activation, and thousands of completed sessions for holdings 5–27. The new scan materializes those later histories before activating holding 4. The base scan never returns or decodes them. Expected bounded work under the writer lock. The SQL-count tests miss this regression because their large batch contains minimal history.
- hotwatch_service.py:899–908 can skip the first eligible holding. Reproduce with an idle tenant whose fifth holding has a linked automatic watch and a later tenant with a due holding. Commit an unrelated update to trigger the idle refresh. After the refreshed batch containing holdings four and five is fetched, reconcile holding five as closed and restore it in the snapshot. The cached LINKED state skips its now-due POSITION_CLOSED generation, and the later tenant gets the tick’s sole activation. The per-position path would see the closure before evaluating holding five and select its new generation first.
- hotwatch_service.py:814–914 changes activation order. Seed a killed user with two eligible holdings and clear the kill switch from a second SQLite connection immediately after the first gate read. The baseline skips the first holding and activates the second. The new loop restarts the tenant and activates the first, consuming the tick’s only activation. Preserve the per-position resume order and test this case. The same idle rescan also raises reads from 3 to 5 per tenant with one retry-deferred holding, no active session, and an unrelated commit during the first pass.
- hotwatch_service.py:882–888 forces one batch per position on idle ticks, repeating tenant gate and session lookups. The deferred-history branch also probes the same autowatch key twice. In an in-memory SQLite comparison with 100 users, distinct portfolios, and 26 shared assets per user (one PAUSED/LINKED, 25 deferred), scan statements fell from 7,800 to 5,200, but VM instructions rose from 144,185 to 597,923. The idle regression test covers only one holding per user. Expected bounded tenant batching to reduce duplicate reads on multi-holding idle ticks while preserving decisions.
- hotwatch_service.py:788,890–897 regresses the 100-user scan. In an in-memory SQLite comparison of the changed lookup SQL against the base, 100 users with one shared asset, distinct portfolios and one paused/linked watch each went from 6,710 to 20,137 VM steps despite fewer statements. With 100 killed users and 26 holdings each, the gate still ran 2,600 times and steps rose from 26,000 to 213,240. Expected fewer duplicate reads and no material increase in lookup work, with link and kill-switch decisions preserved. The one-position regression test counts statements and misses the SQLite work increase.
